newsitem.title: UK: Weak U.S. durable goods data jolts markets.
newsitem.headline: Weak U.S. durable goods data jolts markets.

text.p: U.S. economic data surprised financial markets on Thursday, sending bourses moving sharply in both directions before investors decided the figures were positive.
An unexpectedly large drop in durable goods orders in August appeared to justify the Federal Reserve's decision this week to hold interest rates unchanged.
The figures prompted some traders to even question whether the Fed would need to tighten credit at all this year to rein in inflationary pressures.

"Durable goods are a volatile figure. But it clearly shows that the economy is losing momentum...and that the Federal Reserve was clearly right in refraining from raising interest rates the other day," Irwin Kellner, chief economist, at Chase Regional Bank in New York said.
Profit-taking swiftly wiped out Wall Street's opening gain, but by the time European bourses closed, the Dow Industrial Average was back in positive territory.
The dollar ended higher in Europe, buoyed by mark weakness across the board and a Swiss franc slide following a surprise Swiss rate cut.
Some profit-taking and technical resistance in the mid-1.52 mark region took some of the froth off the dollar's rise but dealers said the U.S. unit was set for more gains.

"The dollar looks well bid, helped by the weaker Swiss franc and the general softness of the mark," said Jeremy Stretch, currency strategist at NatWest Markets. "It has been hit by some profit-taking but there are buyers out there at lower levels."
By 1530 GMT the U.S. currency was quoted at 1.5214 marks and 110.41 yen, compared with late Wednesday's European level of 1.5112 marks and 110.40 yen.

Gold was hit by the head of the International Monetary Fund, Michel Camdessus, saying the fund had the necessary majority to sell five million ounces of bullion from its reserves to help the world's poorest nations.
Gold fixed in London at its lowest price since September 6, 1995 at $380.45 an ounce, down from $382.05 at the morning fix, and closed in London at $380.15.
Europe's major bourses, which had been cautious ahead of the U.S. data, searched for direction as the Dow gyrated.
But Italy's markets had no doubts. They soared to record highs as international investors piled into bonds and the lira, betting on a tough budget in Italy's dash to join European monetary union.
German shares held up at near record high levels, but dealers bemoaned weak trading volumes and were divided on whether the market's bull run could continue.

Gains by government bonds following the U.S. data, kept the 30-share IBIS DAX index up and it closed up 1.86 points at 2,664.96. Earlier the DAX ended floor trade up 7.58 points at 2,666.55 but off its intra-day highs.
Some dealers warned of impending vertigo, with one Frankfurt dealer saying: "People are starting to get cold feet. I really think we have shot up too quickly."
British shares struggled through the afternoon and were able to recoup all their losses by the end, closing down 2.9 points at 3,932.8.
Selective profit-taking in retail stocks helped drag the market down, while drugs company Zeneca dropped after Bayer ruled out a bid.
France's blue chip CAC-40 index spent most of the day weighed down by a handful of heavyweight stocks that reported disappointing first-half results.
Luxury-goods group LVMH fell 3.9 percent on a disappointing rise in first-half profit, but Alcatel Alsthom ended up 2.49 percent at 411 francs.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The U.S. currency was quoted at 1.5214 marks and 110.41 yen, compared with late Wednesday's European level of 1.5112 marks and 110.40 yen.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares closed down 2.5 points, or 0.06 percent, at 3,933.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index closed up 0.73 points, or 0.03 percent, at 2,104.14.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 7.58 points at 2.666.55. In computerised trade, the IBIS DAX ended up 1.86 points, or 0.07 percent, at 2,664.96.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $380.15 against $382.65 previously. Silver ended at $4.89, down three cents.
